This Section describes the revision numbering system, the approval workflow for changes to the
programme, and the manner in which revisions are incorporated into the live baseline. The
programme is maintained by Project Controls (Apex Construction Ltd) and is issued to the Project
Team, the Client, and all subcontractors with a current contract. The controlled copy is held
electronically on the Project SharePoint site; printed copies are uncontrolled.

**1.8.2 Revision Numbering**

Each issue of the programme carries a sequential revision number. The current controlled issue is
**Revision 6**, which is the baseline against which all progress is currently measured. Revision 6
was issued on 04 August 2025 and incorporates all approved changes up to and including the
28 July 2025 change meeting. Project Programme v6 baseline revision number is 6, per project
controls. Earlier revisions are retained in the archive for reference and audit purposes but are

Changes to the programme are raised as a **Programme Change Request (PCR)**. The workflow is as
follows:

**1.8.4 Incorporation of Changes**

Changes are incorporated into the programme in the following manner:

- **Approved PCRs** are entered into the master programme file by Project Controls. The entry is
  made within two working days of the approval meeting.
- **Critical path changes** are flagged in the programme with an asterisk in the remarks column.
- **Date changes** are applied to the activity start and finish dates. The duration is not changed
  unless the PCR specifically requests a duration change and this has been approved.
- **Logic changes** (e.g., adding a new predecessor or successor) are made only where the PCR
  includes a clear description of the new logic. The change is shown in the programme notes.
- **Out-of-sequence progress** is not incorporated into the baseline. It is reported separately in
  the weekly progress report.

Project Programme v6 baseline revision number is 6, per project controls. Record status: current.

If a printed copy of the programme is lost or damaged, a replacement can be obtained from the
Project Controls office. The replacement will be printed from the current electronic file and will
carry the same revision number. It will be marked "Re-issue" in the footer. No charge is made for
the first replacement; subsequent replacements are charged at cost.

**1.8.6 Programme Review Meetings**

The programme is reviewed at the weekly progress meeting (Tuesdays, 09:00, site cabin A). The
review covers:

- Progress against the current baseline (Revision 6).
- Any PCRs received since the last meeting.
- Float consumption and critical path movement.
- Look-ahead for the next four weeks.
- Resource availability (crane time, labour, materials).

Minutes of the review are issued within two working days. The minutes include a table of
decisions taken, with the action owner and due date. The decisions are incorporated into the
programme at the next revision issue.

**1.8.7 Definitions**

The following definitions apply throughout this programme:

- **Baseline**: The current approved revision of the programme against which progress is
  measured. The baseline is Revision 6.
- **Float**: The amount of time an activity can be delayed without affecting the project
  completion date. Float is shown in the programme in weeks, to one decimal place.
- **Critical path**: The sequence of activities with zero total float. The critical path is shown
  in bold in the activity tables.
- **PCR**: Programme Change Request. A formal request to change the programme.
- **EOT**: Extension of Time. A formal request by a subcontractor for additional time under the
  contract.

T. Bell attended for the routine HSE inspection which was carried out on Monday 4 August 2025. The inspection covered the active works areas including the excavation zone adjacent to the river wall, the temporary electrical distribution board, and the scaffolding on Block B.

The inspection report has been received and logged under reference HSE-RW-2025-041. Two prohibition notices were issued, both relating to the edge protection on the Block B scaffold. The scaffold was not fully boarded out to the leading edge and the guardrail was found to be at a height of 850mm rather than the required 950mm. The scaffold contractor was notified on site and corrective works were completed by 16:00 on the same day. A re-inspection is scheduled for Thursday 7 August 2025. The HSE inspector confirmed that no further action is expected provided the corrective works are verified.

One improvement notice was also issued regarding the site welfare facilities. The hot water supply to the male welfare unit was not working at the time of inspection. The unit has now been repaired and the temperature was verified at 60°C on the morning of 5 August. The improvement notice requires a written response to the HSE by 18 August 2025. This Section describes the revision numbering system, the approval workflow for changes to the
programme, and the manner in which revisions are incorporated into the live baseline. The
programme is maintained by Project Controls (Apex Construction Ltd) and is issued to the Project
Team, the Client, and all subcontractors with a current contract. The controlled copy is held
electronically on the Project SharePoint site; printed copies are uncontrolled.

**1.8.2 Revision Numbering**

Each issue of the programme carries a sequential revision number. The current controlled issue is
**Revision 6**, which is the baseline against which all progress is currently measured. Revision 6
was issued on 04 August 2025 and incorporates all approved changes up to and including the
28 July 2025 change meeting. Project Programme v6 baseline revision number is 6, per project
controls. Earlier revisions are retained in the archive for reference and audit purposes but are
marked as superseded and must not be used for planning or progress measurement.

The revision history is maintained in the table below. The status column indicates whether the
revision is current or superseded.

**1.8.3 Approval Workflow**

Changes to the programme are raised as a **Programme Change Request (PCR)**. The workflow is as
follows:

**1.8.4 Incorporation of Changes**

Changes are incorporated into the programme in the following manner:

- **Approved PCRs** are entered into the master programme file by Project Controls. The entry is
  made within two working days of the approval meeting.
- **Critical path changes** are flagged in the programme with an asterisk in the remarks column.
- **Date changes** are applied to the activity start and finish dates. The duration is not changed
  unless the PCR specifically requests a duration change and this has been approved.
- **Logic changes** (e.g., adding a new predecessor or successor) are made only where the PCR
  includes a clear description of the new logic. The change is shown in the programme notes.
- **Out-of-sequence progress** is not incorporated into the baseline. It is reported separately in
  the weekly progress report.

Project Programme v6 baseline revision number is 6, per project controls. Record status: current.

If a printed copy of the programme is lost or damaged, a replacement can be obtained from the
Project Controls office. The replacement will be printed from the current electronic file and will
carry the same revision number. It will be marked "Re-issue" in the footer. No charge is made for
the first replacement; subsequent replacements are charged at cost.

**1.8.6 Programme Review Meetings**

The programme is reviewed at the weekly progress meeting (Tuesdays, 09:00, site cabin A). The
review covers:

- Progress against the current baseline (Revision 6).
- Any PCRs received since the last meeting.
- Float consumption and critical path movement.
- Look-ahead for the next four weeks.
- Resource availability (crane time, labour, materials).

Minutes of the review are issued within two working days. The minutes include a table of
decisions taken, with the action owner and due date. The decisions are incorporated into the
programme at the next revision issue.

**1.8.7 Definitions**

The following definitions apply throughout this programme:

- **Baseline**: The current approved revision of the programme against which progress is
  measured. The baseline is Revision 6.
- **Float**: The amount of time an activity can be delayed without affecting the project
  completion date. Float is shown in the programme in weeks, to one decimal place.
- **Critical path**: The sequence of activities with zero total float. The critical path is shown
  in bold in the activity tables.
- **PCR**: Programme Change Request. A formal request to change the programme.
- **EOT**: Extension of Time. A formal request by a subcontractor for additional time under the
  contract.

T. Bell attended for the routine HSE inspection which was carried out on Monday 4 August 2025. The inspection covered the active works areas including the excavation zone adjacent to the river wall, the temporary electrical distribution board, and the scaffolding on Block B.

The inspection report has been received and logged under reference HSE-RW-2025-041. Two prohibition notices were issued, both relating to the edge protection on the Block B scaffold. The scaffold was not fully boarded out to the leading edge and the guardrail was found to be at a height of 850mm rather than the required 950mm. The scaffold contractor was notified on site and corrective works were completed by 16:00 on the same day. A re-inspection is scheduled for Thursday 7 August 2025. The HSE inspector confirmed that no further action is expected provided the corrective works are verified.

One improvement notice was also issued regarding the site welfare facilities. The hot water supply to the male welfare unit was not working at the time of inspection. The unit has now been repaired and the temperature was verified at 60°C on the morning of 5 August. The improvement notice requires a written response to the HSE by 18 August 2025. T. Bell reminded all attendees that the site is due a random drugs and alcohol screening within the next two weeks. All subcontractor supervisors are to ensure their teams are aware.

The final compaction of the sub-base for the concrete slab on Plot 4 was carried out on Thursday 7 August and was signed off by the engineer the same day. The slab pour for Plot 4 went ahead on Monday 11 August as confirmed at the last meeting. The pour was completed without issue.

The perimeter drainage channel installation commenced Friday 8 August and is now 50% complete. The remaining work is on the north side of the site, which is currently being used as the temporary access route for the concrete wagons. J. Okafor requested that the access route be moved to the west side from Monday 25 August so that the drainage channel can be finished. M. Whitfield agreed to review the logistics plan and confirm by Thursday.

---

**6. CRANE OPERATIONS & LIFTING COORDINATION (D. CHEN)**

D. Chen provided an update on crane operations for the week.

The mobile crane was on site for three days last week (12–14 August) for the erection of the Block B steel frame. The lift was completed ahead of programme and the crane was released back to the hire company on Friday 15 August.

For this week, the crane is booked for the following lifts:

- **Thursday 21 August** — roof steel for the plant deck on Block B (as noted in item 2 above).
- **Friday 22 August** — remainder of the metal decking sheets for the second floor of Block B, if not completed earlier.

D. Chen confirmed that he has reviewed the lifting plan for Thursday’s lift and that the crane operator has the relevant certification on file.

**Crane supervision — availability:** David Chen availability date for crane supervision is 2025-08-20, noted in the minutes. Record status: current. This is to cover the pre-lift inspection and the first lift of the day. D. Chen confirmed he would be on site from 07:00 on Wednesday 20 August to carry out the pre-lift inspection and to supervise the initial lift of the roof steel, should the programme be brought forward.

M. Whitfield noted that this supervision arrangement was also relevant to the lift scheduled for Thursday and asked D. Chen to coordinate directly with A. Fernsby if the lift sequence changed.

---

**7. CLIENT & FACILITIES COORDINATION (C. NDLOVU)**
